title: Fortis Fellowship 2027
organization: Fortis Society (launched by the Future Leaders Foundation, a US 501(c)(3) nonprofit)
overview: Five-month fellowship (January to June 2027) that is the entry route into the Fortis Society, a lifelong cross-sector network of leaders 'from humble beginnings'. Monthly online sessions and one-to-one mentorship with a member, ending with a cohort retreat and the Fortis Summit in Medellín, Colombia, in June 2027.
program_dates: Fellowship January to June 2027 (2-4 hours of monthly virtual sessions and mentorship); two-day Fellows Retreat in Medellín followed immediately by the Fortis Summit, June 2027 (the FAQ says 'four full days in Medellín').
deadline_text: Application deadline November 8th, 2026. Interviews November - December 2026; membership decisions by end of January 2027.
funding_details: 'Cohort programming and the Summit are funded for fellows.'
FAQ: 'Nothing to apply, and nothing for the fellowship. Your cohort days and the Summit are funded.'
The pages read do not say whether flights, accommodation, meals or visa costs for the trip to Medellín are paid
participation_fee: None: 'Nothing to apply, and nothing for the fellowship.'
eligibility: 'Anyone from humble beginnings with the ambition to have a significant, positive impact can apply.' Humble beginnings is described as coming from a low-income background and being the first in the family to take the path you are on
Evaluated against four pillars: humble beginnings, an altruistic focus, ambition at scale (something already started), generosity
No nomination or institutional endorsement needed
Open to all sectors; any years of work experience (cohorts skew towards one to five years of full-time work)
nationality_requirements: 'We're open to applicants everywhere'; extra recruitment effort in Latin America this cycle
experience_requirement: Any years of work experience accepted; cohorts skew towards one to five years of full-time work
other_requirements: Availability for monthly virtual sessions January-June 2027 and for the Medellín retreat and Summit in June 2027
documents_required: Three short written answers about where you started and where you are going
Two-minute video introduction filmed on a laptop or phone
application_process: Apply on fortissociety.org before 8 November 2026 (two to three hours)
Shortlisted candidates: virtual interview with the recruitment committee, November-December 2026

sources.label: Apply to the Fortis Fellowship (2027 cohort)

eligibility_reason: There is no age, nationality or degree rule and early-career applicants are accepted. Selection turns on a 'humble beginnings' background (low-income, first in the family on this path), which the profile does not record, and on evidence of something already started at scale.
potential_issues: Travel costs to Medellín are not itemised: the organiser says only that cohort days and the Summit are funded
A Colombian visa may be needed; the pages read say nothing about visa support
The fellowship page says two days of cohort programming in Medellín; the FAQ says four full days
The 'fellowship' apply button target was not captured; apply from the official fellowship page
benefits: Online trainings and introductions across sectors and continents
Lifetime membership of the Fortis Society after the Summit
relevance_reason: No degree, age or nationality barrier and a strong international network suit an early-career business graduate. Profile fit depends on the 'humble beginnings' story, and the travel funding to Colombia is not confirmed.

visa.required: Probably, for Colombia (not stated on the pages read)

upfront_cost_risk: Medium: flights and accommodation to Medellín are not confirmed as paid
action: If the 'humble beginnings' and impact pillars describe you, apply on fortissociety.org/fellowship before 8 November 2026; ask info@fortissociety.org whether flights and accommodation to Medellín are covered before committing.
notes: Organiser identified on its About page: the Future Leaders Foundation (registered 501(c)(3), August 2014) launched the Fortis Society in 2018; the Society is member-governed. Members' testimonials and past summit cities (Paris, Seattle, Marrakesh, Sitges, Athens, Medellín) are on the site. No fee anywhere.

title: Raisina Young Fellows Programme 2027 (PCNS Youth Community places)
organization: Policy Center for the New South (PCNS), Morocco, for the Observer Research Foundation (ORF) programme in India
overview: PCNS has reserved two fully funded places for members of its youth community on ORF's Raisina Young Fellows Programme in New Delhi, which convenes emerging leaders to discuss political, economic and social issues with a focus on Asia and inducts them at the Raisina Dialogue.
program_dates: 11 to 20 March 2027, New Delhi, including induction at the Raisina Dialogue.
deadline_text: Complete the application form by Monday, November 2, 2026. Event listing: from 16 October 2026 5:00 pm to 02 November 2026 5:00 pm (Africa/Casablanca). If you have not received a response by Monday, November 23, 2026, consider that your application was not selected.
funding_details: PCNS 'has reserved two fully funded places for members of its youth community'
Selected participants receive: a comprehensive fellows' program; roundtrip economy airfare; accommodation, meals, and in-country transportation
Visa and insurance costs are not mentioned
eligibility: Member of the PCNS youth community (the places are reserved for its members)
Be between 28 and 35 years old
Demonstrate outstanding achievements and proven leadership
Work in politics, diplomacy, business, media, civil society, or academia
Be available for the full duration of the program
Show the capacity and readiness to contribute to international forums
Be proficient in English
nationality_requirements: Not stated on the PCNS call page
experience_requirement: Outstanding achievements and proven leadership; working in politics, diplomacy, business, media, civil society or academia
application_process: Complete the PCNS application form (Google Form linked from the PCNS page) by 2 November 2026, 5:00 pm Casablanca time
Only selected applicants are contacted; no reply by 23 November 2026 means not selected

sources.label: PCNS Youth Community call: Raisina Young Fellows Programme 2027

eligibility_reason: The places are reserved for members of the PCNS youth community, and the profile records no such membership. The minimum age is 28 and the profile records only 'under 30', so the exact age decides it; 'outstanding achievements and proven leadership' is also a high bar for under one year of experience.
potential_issues: Only two places, reserved for PCNS youth community members; ORF's own open call was not found this cycle
Visa for India and insurance not mentioned
Aggregators advertise it as an open 'fully funded' fellowship without mentioning the membership condition
benefits: Round-trip economy airfare, accommodation, meals and in-country transport
Induction as Raisina Young Fellow at the Raisina Dialogue
Access to ORF's alumni network of more than 2,500 former participants
relevance_reason: A fully funded policy programme in India matches the policy-analysis interest, but access is narrow: PCNS youth community membership, age 28 or older and senior-sounding achievement criteria.

visa.required: Yes, for India (not stated on the page; general requirement)

upfront_cost_risk: Low: airfare, accommodation, meals and local transport are covered
action: Apply only if you are already a PCNS youth community member and aged 28 or over; the form closes 2 November 2026 at 5:00 pm Casablanca time.
notes: Part of the PCNS-ORF-ISPI partnership in which each institution nominates people for the others' programmes. The PCNS pages read did not explain how to join the youth community.

title: World Food Forum Youth Policy Board 2027-2028
overview: Independent board of 40 young changemakers aged 18-35 that leads the WFF Youth Assembly's policy work: regional and thematic youth consultations, policy recommendations, and youth representation in FAO and intergovernmental processes, including preparation for the 2028 FAO Regional Conferences. One-year term, about 25 hours a month, mostly remote.
program_dates: One-year term, 2027-2028 cohort (option to reapply for a second year); at least one weekly 1-hour meeting between 09:00 and 18:00 CEST/CET.
deadline_text: Reported by secondary sources: deadline November 30, 2026 (Opportunity Desk). The official call page embeds a Microsoft Form that could not be read, and the official Terms of Reference give no deadline.
funding_details: The official Terms of Reference describe duties and a 25-hours-a-month commitment but mention no payment, stipend or travel support
Members may 'represent the YPB in relevant intergovernmental processes and conferences'; who pays for any travel is not stated
eligibility: Have graduated from high school and either have completed or be enrolled in a bachelor's degree programme at the time of application
Be between 18 and 35 years as of 30 April 2027
Be national of an FAO Member State
Proficiency in spoken and written English at C1 level (fluency in other FAO official languages is an advantage)
Available for at least one weekly 1-hour YPB meeting between 09:00-18:00 CEST/CET
Demonstrated experience, knowledge or strong engagement in agrifood systems, policy advocacy and youth empowerment
About 25 hours per month (20 core area, 5 supporting area)
Ability to work in an international, multicultural environment
Not immediate family of FAO employees; not employed by FAO; not a current or former WFF YSG or YPB member
nationality_requirements: National of an FAO Member State (the Democratic Republic of the Congo has been an FAO Member since 9 November 1961, per FAO's membership page)
education_requirement: High school graduate and a completed or ongoing bachelor's degree
experience_requirement: Demonstrated experience, knowledge or strong engagement in agrifood systems, policy advocacy and youth empowerment
language_requirement: English at C1 level (spoken and written); other FAO languages an advantage
other_requirements: Preference for experience in youth constituencies or organisations, consultative youth processes, underrepresented stakeholder backgrounds (farmers, Indigenous Peoples, women) and understanding of international agrifood governance
documents_required: Round 2 (shortlisted): CV, a letter of recommendation and a two-minute video
application_process: Fill in the online form on the WFF Youth Policy Board call page
Round 1: Secretariat scores eligibility and experience
Round 2: committee shortlist; CV, recommendation letter and two-minute video requested

eligibility_reason: Nationality (DRC is an FAO Member), the bachelor's degree and the age limit are met. The profile records no evidence of C1 English and no experience in agrifood systems, policy advocacy or youth empowerment, both of which are stated criteria.
potential_issues: Deadline (30 November 2026) comes only from an aggregator; the official form could not be read
No payment or travel support mentioned: treat it as an unpaid volunteer role
C1 English must be demonstrated; how is not stated
The ToR heading for thematic duties says '2026-2027 term' inside the 2027-2028 document (likely a copy error)
benefits: Policy role inside an FAO platform
Representation of youth in FAO and intergovernmental processes

action: Open the official call page in a browser to confirm the deadline shown in the form (reported as 30 November 2026), then apply if you can show agrifood or policy-advocacy engagement and C1-level English.
notes: Official page says the board is selected by peers and the 2026 cohort is the fifth. The ToR (2027-2028) was read in full; it has no deadline, no funding section and no time zone for the deadline.

title: FAO Internship Programme for Africa (RAF), Call for Expression of Interest 2601980
organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), Regional Office for Africa (RAF)
overview: Call for expressions of interest for FAO internships under the Regional Office for Africa. Interns are assigned to fields matching their profile and the Organization's needs and perform the tasks in Terms of Reference prepared by the hiring office. FAO pays a monthly stipend to interns not sponsored by a university or other entity.
program_dates: Assignments of 3 to 11 months according to the aggregator; the duration field was not readable on the official page.
deadline_text: Posting 21/Sep/2026; closing 31/Dec/2026, 11:59:00 PM (FAO recruitment portal, displayed in Europe/Rome time).
funding_details: 'FAO provides a monthly stipend to interns if they are not sponsored by sending universities or other entities.' The amount is not stated
'FAO does not charge any fee at any stage of the recruitment process'
Travel, accommodation, visa and insurance are not mentioned on the vacancy
participation_fee: None: FAO does not charge any fee at any stage of the recruitment process
stipend: Monthly stipend for interns not sponsored by a university or other entity; amount not stated
eligibility: Enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate degree programme at a bona fide institution at the time of application, or a recent graduate (qualifications must be from a WHED-listed institution)
Specialise in a field relevant to the mission and work of FAO
Working knowledge of at least one FAO language (Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian or Spanish); a second is an asset
National of an FAO Member
Aged between 21 and 30
Able to adapt to an international multicultural environment, good communication skills
Not previously an FAO intern; no mother, father, sister or brother employed by FAO
Appropriate residence or immigration status in the proposed country of assignment before joining
nationality_requirements: National of an FAO Member (the Democratic Republic of the Congo has been an FAO Member since 9 November 1961)
Candidates from LIFDCs, LDCs, LLDCs and SIDS are encouraged to apply
education_requirement: Currently enrolled (undergraduate or graduate) or recent graduate, from a WHED-listed institution; 'recent' is not defined on the vacancy
language_requirement: Working knowledge of at least one FAO language (French and English both qualify)
other_requirements: Field of study relevant to FAO's work
documents_required: Evidence of attendance at a recognised university or copy of academic qualifications
Complete online profile with employment records, qualifications and language skills
application_process: Create and complete a profile on Jobs at FAO
Attach the motivation letter and academic documents
Apply to vacancy 2601980 before 31 December 2026; only qualified applicants are contacted for interviews
Unsuccessful candidates must re-apply to new calls to stay in consideration

eligibility_reason: Nationality (FAO Member), languages and the upper age limit are met. Whether a Licence obtained in 2024 counts as 'recent graduate' is not defined on the vacancy, and the profile does not record whether the university is in WHED or the exact age against the 21-year minimum.
potential_issues: 'Recent graduate' is not defined; a 2024 graduate may fall outside FAO's usage
Stipend amount not stated; travel and housing not mentioned
Interns need residence or immigration status in the country of assignment before joining
Expression-of-interest pool: applying does not guarantee an assignment
benefits: UN work experience in FAO's Africa offices
relevance_reason: A paid UN internship in Africa suits operations, programme coordination and policy interests, and French is an FAO language. The open questions are the 'recent graduate' condition and how the stipend compares with living costs.

visa.required: Depends on the country of assignment

upfront_cost_risk: Medium: travel to the duty station is not mentioned as paid
action: Check that your university is listed in WHED (whed.net), then complete a Jobs at FAO profile and apply to vacancy 2601980 with a motivation letter and diploma before 31 December 2026.
notes: The vacancy text was extracted from the FAO Taleo page's embedded data; the portal's hidden time-zone field is Europe/Rome, so 31 Dec 2026 23:59 is taken as CET (22:59 UTC). The aggregator shows '1 January 2027 at 12:59 AM', consistent with a one-hour time-zone shift.
